newsitem.title: EGYPT: Eastern share offer fully subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Eastern share offer fully subscribed.

text.p: A privatisation offer of five million shares in Egyptian cigarette manufacturer Eastern Company is probably heavily oversubscribed, the agents for the sale said on Tuesday.
"We alone have applications for the five million and we haven't yet seen the orders from other brokers," said an official at brokers EFG-Hermes.
The prices in the applications are mostly in the range 96 to 98 pounds ($28.28 to $28.87) a share, he added. The minimum price was 96 pounds.
The five million shares represent 20 percent of the equity in Eastern Company, which has a monopoly of cigarette production in Egypt.

The seller is the state's Holding Company for Mining and Refractories, which owns 80 percent of the shares after selling 10 percent to the private sector in June 1995. The company employees own the remaining 10 percent.
The sale is expected to go through the stock exchange on Wednesday, the official said.
The shares closed on the Egyptian stock exchange at 100.00 pounds on Monday.
